thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Soars 290 Points, but Check Out the Little Guys - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Soars 290 Points, but Check Out the Little Guys - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends May 30, 2018 12:57 p.m. ET The Dow Jones Industrial Average is soaring today as the market puts Italy and China trade tensions behind it. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Bloomberg News •...marvel at the big gains in small stocks;
•...observe that Microsoft (MSFT) is now worth more than Alphabet (GOOGL);
•...highlight the nearly 20% drop in Chico's Fas (CHS).
Stocks U.S. stocks shrugged off Italy and China fears Wednesday morning and charged higher , as risk and reflation were back on the menu.
For now, anyway.
Rising stocks outnumbered falling ones by a hefty 4-to-1 on U.S. exchanges, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 290 points while the S&P 500 rose 1.3%. Ten-year Treasury yields jumped nearly 0.09 percentage point, to 2.85%, while oil jumped $1.60 and most industrial metal prices were trading higher.
All that panic about Italy? That was yesterday.
If you think the headline indexes are impressive, you should take a look at smaller stocks . Small-caps hit records, with the Russell 2000 small cap index rising 1.6%. John Lynch, chief investment strategist at LPL Financial, says that the technicals are pointing toward further gains: The index has broken out above its long-term upward trend line, after successfully holding above the trend at the February lows. Make of that what you will.
Charles Bilello, director of research at Pension Partners, points out that even U.S. micro-caps, which are smaller than mere small-caps, are joining the party. U.S. micro-caps are “at a new all-time high,” he noted on Twitter, adding that the iShares Micro-cap ETF (IWC), which tracks the Russell Microcap index, is up nearly 10% so far this year, while the iShares S&P 100 ETF (OEF), which tracks the 100 biggest companies, is up only 1%.
In other news, Microsoft (MSFT), up 0.9%, is now more valuable than Alphabet (GOOGL), up 0.8%. This follows a year of sustained outperformance. But at $760 billion, Microsoft still has a long way to go to catch Apple (AAPL), down 0.4%, which is valued at $920 billion.
Midday Movers Allergan (AGN) is down 0.7% to $149.92 on news that it will put its women's-health and infectious-diseases businesses up for sale .
Chico's Fas (CHS) is down 19.7% to $8.02 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The apparel retailer earned 23 cents a share on revenue of $561.8 million. Analysts were looking for EPS of 26 cents on revenue of $551.99 million. For the full year, it warned that it expects a mid-single decline in net sales and a low-to-mid single decline in comparable sales.
DSW (DSW) is down 8.9% to $23.75 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The shoe seller earned 39 cents a share on revenue of $712.1million. Analysts were looking for earnings of 37 cents a share on revenue of $683.8 million. For the full year, DSW expects EPS of $1.52 to $1.67, compared with the $1.62 consensus estimate.
Monster Beverage (MNST) is up 4.5% to $51.51 after its board of directors authorized a new $500 million share-repurchase plan.
Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is up 1% to $209.88 after Stifel upgraded it to Buy. — Teresa Rivas
